worked_solution:
Using the transformation $y=v(x)x$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x) \\  & =x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the differential equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{{y}^{3}}{x{y}^{2}+{x}^{3}} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v & =\frac{(vx)^{3}}{x(vx)^{2}+{x}^{3}} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v & =\frac{{v}^{3}{x}^{3}}{({v}^{2}+1){x}^{3}} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v & =\frac{{v}^{3}}{{v}^{2}+1} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{{v}^{3}}{{v}^{2}+1}-v \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{{v}^{3}-{v}^{3}-v}{{v}^{2}+1} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =-\frac{v}{{v}^{2}+1} \\ \frac{{v}^{2}+1}{v}\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =-\frac{1}{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Integrating both sides with respect to $x$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{v}^{2}+1}{v}\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =-\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x \\ \int (v+\frac{1}{v})\,\text{d}v & =-\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x \\ \frac{{v}^{2}}{2}+\operatorname{ln}⁡|v| & =-\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|+{C}_{1} \\ {v}^{2}+2\operatorname{ln}⁡|v| & =-2\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|+2{C}_{1} \\ {v}^{2}+\operatorname{ln}⁡({v}^{2}) & =-\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2})+C.\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that we introduced $C=2{C}_{1}.$

From the transformation $y=vx$, we get

$$
v=\frac{y}{x}.
$$

Finally, substituting the above into our solution, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{(\frac{y}{x})}^{2}+\operatorname{ln}⁡{(\frac{y}{x})}^{2} & =-\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2})+C \\ \frac{{y}^{2}}{{x}^{2}}+\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{{y}^{2}}{{x}^{2}}) & =-\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2})+C \\ \frac{{y}^{2}}{{x}^{2}}+\operatorname{ln}⁡({y}^{2})-\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}) & =-\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2})+C \\ \frac{{y}^{2}}{{x}^{2}}+\operatorname{ln}⁡({y}^{2}) & =C \\ \frac{{y}^{2}}{{x}^{2}} & =C-\operatorname{ln}⁡({y}^{2}) \\ \frac{{y}^{2}}{C-\operatorname{ln}⁡({y}^{2})} & ={x}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
